# dsh-deeptutor
**English** | 简体中文

A **learning-assistant extension for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) and Claude Code**.
It connects your agen

t to a HKUDS/DeepTutor
tutoring service, so a session can explain topics in depth, quiz you, plan
le

arning paths, search your personal knowledge bases, and keep a study
notebook, all without leaving t

he agent. In dsh it loads as a bundle; in
Claude Code (or any MCP client) the same tools are served

by a bundled MCP
server, installed as a Claude Code plugin.

Ask the agent *"teach me async/await"* and it can run a deep-solve, render the
answer as a self-cont

ained HTML study page you can open in a browser, and
archive a summary into your notebook.
## What it adds
Four agent-facing tools that the model uses whenever you ask for learning help:
| Tool | What it does |
| `deeptutor_run` | Runs one learning capability, e.g. `deep_solve` (in-depth explanation), `deep_qu
estion` (self-test questions), `deep_research`, `chat`, `mastery_path` (learning-path planning), `vi
sualize`. Can mount your knowledge bases (`kbs`) and tools (`rag`, `web_search`, `reason`, `code_exe
cution`, …); returns a `session_id` so later turns continue the same context, and can render the ans

wer to an HTML study page. |
| `deeptutor_kb` | Lists, searches, and inspects your personal knowledg

e bases (RAG) |
| `deeptutor_note` | Archives Markdown study notes (plans, summaries, wrong answers)

into a server notebook |
| `deeptutor_cli` | Runs any other DeepTutor CLI command, behind safety ti

r notebook |
| `deeptutor_cli` | Runs any other DeepTutor CLI command, behind safety tiers (below) |
### Following DeepTutor upgrades without plugin releases

The plugin does not mirror DeepTutor's command surface, so a DeepTutor upgrade
that adds commands, c
apabilities or tools needs no plugin change:

- **Capabilities are discovered at runtime.** `deeptutor_run` takes any
capability name. The plugin

reads `deeptutor module list` (JSON, cached for
five minutes) to learn which capabilities the deploy

ment's ready modules
provide; a capability whose module is not ready fails fast with the reason and

the list of available ones, and names no module lists are passed straight to
the CLI (they may come

from a DeepTutor plugin).
- **Every other command goes through `deeptutor_cli`.** The agent discover

s
commands from the CLI itself (`args: ["--help"]`, then `["kb", "--help"]`, …)
instead of a list ba

ked into the plugin. Safety tiers keep the passthrough
honest about commands it has never seen:
| Tier | Commands | Behaviour |
| read | `--help`, verbs `list` / `show` / `info` / `search` / `state` / `status` / `list-*`, `docto

r`, `run` | runs directly |
| confirm | everything else, including verbs the plugin does not know ye
t | runs only with `confirm: true`, which the agent may set only after you explicitly asked for that

change |
| blocked | `delete`, `remove*`, `clear`, `uninstall`, `rollback`, `login`, …; interactive
or long-running `chat` / `start` / `stop` / `serve` / `init` | refused; run them in a terminal your
ng-running `chat` / `start` / `stop` / `serve` / `init` | refused; run them in a terminal yourself |

- **Drift check.** Only the few CLI shapes the dedicated tools are built on
(`run --format json` eve

nts, `kb search`, `notebook add-md`, `module list`)
can break the plugin. `npm run check:cli` checks

them against the deployment
your env vars point at; run it after upgrading DeepTutor.
## Example session
A typical flow when you ask your agent for learning help:
1. **Ask** — *"Explain C# generics covariance using my dotnet knowledge base, and generate a study p

age."*
2. The agent grounds the answer in your own material: `deeptutor_kb` (`action=search`, `kb=do

tnet`).
3. It runs a deep-solve: `deeptutor_run` (`capability=deep_solve`, `kbs=[dotnet]`, `html=dat
a/study/csharp-covariance.html`) — the answer comes back and a self-contained HTML page (plus the `.

md` source) is written to disk.
4. It files a summary: `deeptutor_note` (`notebook=dotnet-learning`,

written to disk.
4. It files a summary: `deeptutor_note` (`notebook=dotnet-learning`, `type=solve`).

Nothing here is a fixed script — the agent picks the tools and parameters based
on what you ask for.

## Requirements

- An agent host: Claude Code (or another MCP client) with Node ≥ 20, or a
working DeepSeek Harness (

dsh) install, 0.1.0-rc.6 or newer. The manifest
declares a version floor rather than a ceiling, so a

new dsh release is never
refused at install time; a scheduled probe boots the plugin against the
cu

rrent npm `latest` and `next` hosts instead and opens an issue when
activation breaks. Bundle auto-r

egistration via `dsh plugin add` was verified
on dsh CLI 0.1.0-rc.6, 0.2.1-rc.2 and 0.2.1-rc.3.
- A

DeepTutor deployment, either:
- **Local** — the `deeptutor` CLI installed on this machine (on `PATH`

ach with
passwordless SSH; the plugin runs the server's CLI over SSH.

Tested against DeepTutor 1.7.1. Since 1.7 the `kb` and `notebook` commands
and most capabilities com

e from optional modules; check that the ones you
use are installed and enabled with `deeptutor modul

ptional modules; check that the ones you
use are installed and enabled with `deeptutor module list`.
## How it works

Every tool call drives the DeepTutor CLI: the local `deeptutor` binary, or the
remote binary over SS

H when `DEEPTUTOR_SSH_HOST` is set. `deeptutor serve` does
not need to be reachable from this machin

when `DEEPTUTOR_SSH_HOST` is set. `deeptutor serve` does
not need to be reachable from this machine.

Earlier versions tried the HTTP/WebSocket API first (`/api/v1/...` through an
SSH tunnel) and only t

hen fell back to the CLI. DeepTutor 1.7 serves those
routes under different paths and behind a login

, so the probe always failed
and each call waited about 30 seconds before reaching the CLI. That pat

h was
removed; `DEEPTUTOR_API_BASE` is no longer read.
